prompt.context: Uranus Co. is an aerospace company headquartered in Bangkok that works with both governments and other private companies to provide aerospace equipment and assets. They are considering entering the luxury space travel market, offering an experience similar to a cruise ship. Their biggest competitors are SpaceX and MoonShine. They want to break even within 2 years.
prompt.question: Uranus Co. wants to assess whether the space travel market is lucrative and large enough to enter. Should they enter this market, and can they break even within 2 years?

clarifying_info.q: What is Uranus Co.'s current business?
clarifying_info.a: Uranus works with both governments and other private companies to provide aerospace equipment and assets.
SpaceX and MoonShine are Uranus's biggest competitors.

clarifying_info.q: What kind of experience will they offer?
clarifying_info.a: Similar to a cruise ship experience.
Due to the high price of tickets, they will only be able to sell to millionaires around the globe.

clarifying_info.q: What geographies does Uranus operate in?

clarifying_info.a: Uranus wants to break even in 2 years.

exhibits.title: Market Research
exhibits.shows: A table of market research metrics including global population, percentage of millionaires globally, age and city distribution of millionaires, and a survey of 200 American millionaires covering travel interest, ticket purchase intent, heart conditions, and asthma. A note states the only requirement for travel is no heart conditions.

exhibits.title: Competitive Landscape
exhibits.shows: A pie chart showing market share by number of tickets (SpaceX 50%, MoonShine 30%, Rest of Market 20% with no single company above 6%), and a bar chart comparing SpaceX, MoonShine, and Uranus across five dimensions: Safety, Cost, Distance from Earth, Length of Voyage, and Amenities. Note: shorter bar indicates higher cost.

data.note: Shorter bar on cost axis indicates higher cost

exhibits.title: Customer Surveys
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing customer-rated level of importance (0-10) for five attributes: Cost, Distance from Earth, Length of Trip, Amenities, and Safety. Accompanied by three customer quotes about their priorities.

customer_quotes: I want the voyage to be longer so I can relax and get my money's worth
The higher we are, the better the view
Cost does not matter to me. I'll pay extra for the best experience

exhibits.title: Operations Information
exhibits.shows: A table of operational metrics for Uranus Co.'s fleet and operations.

exhibits.title: Revenue and Cost Data
exhibits.shows: A table of revenue and cost data including ticket price, other revenue per customer, fixed costs (ship construction, fuel price, maintenance, payroll, launch pad lease, insurance, marketing), and variable cost per customer.

framework: Revenues: ticket sales, food/drinks/merchandise, onboard activities, broadcasting/live stream
Costs — Fixed: spaceships (capital), launch pad permits/leases, insurance, payroll, marketing; Variable: fuel, maintenance, food/drink, wages
Internal capabilities: IP, operational capabilities, financial capacity, brand image
Market: competition (SpaceX, MoonShine, fragmented rest), market shares, strengths/weaknesses
Customers: demographics, preferences for product features (distance, length, amenities, safety), pricing sensitivity
Go-to-Market strategy: organic growth, partnerships, M&A
Product/service definition: price point, length of trip, safety standards, onboard experiences
Regulatory considerations: launch permits, international aerospace regulations

questions.prompt: What factors would you consider in estimating the market size for this service?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify: global population, percentage who are millionaires, health/age requirements for space travel (specifically no heart conditions — asthma and age are red herrings), willingness to travel to space (Yes + Maybe count), and number of tickets per person per year (including family). Strong candidates note that survey responses may be skewed (only American millionaires surveyed, potential dishonesty about health).

questions.prompt: Estimate the total market size of space travel tickets using the market research data provided (Exhibit 1).
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply health filter (no heart conditions) — 125/200 = 62.5%, round to ~5/8 eligible. Asthma and age above 50 are red herrings. Yes and Maybe responses both count as potential market. Strong candidate flags survey limitations: US-only sample of 200 may not represent global millionaire population.

math.setup: Start with global population, filter to millionaires, apply health eligibility, apply willingness, multiply by annual ticket purchases.
steps: Apply health eligibility (no heart conditions): 8M x 5/8 = 5M eligible
Apply willingness to travel (Yes=90, Maybe=30 out of 200 surveyed = 120/200 = 60%): 5M x 60% = 3M
Multiply by average tickets per year: 3M x 2.3 = 6.9M tickets/year

questions.prompt: Based on the competitive landscape and customer preferences (Exhibits 2 and 3), what market share do you think Uranus Co. can capture, and why?
questions.guidance: A good candidate provides a reasoned market share estimate. Key insights: market is fragmented outside top two (20% split among many players each <6%); Uranus leads competitors on all metrics except cost, but customers say cost is unimportant; Uranus should easily capture the fragmented 20% and can siphon from SpaceX and MoonShine over time due to superior offering. A great candidate notes market share capture will be gradual — Uranus must first establish credibility before taking share from established players. Interviewer should let candidate propose before revealing Uranus targets 20% market penetration.

questions.prompt: Does Uranus Co. have the operational capacity to meet a 20% market share target? (Use Exhibit 4)
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate annual ticket capacity and compare to 20% of the 6.9M ticket market. Should recognize Uranus can just barely exceed 20% capacity.

math.setup: Calculate total annual trips, then total tickets per year, then compare to 20% of market.
steps: Trips per year: 2 trips/ship/month x 12 months x 150 ships = 3,600 trips/year
Tickets per year: 400 passengers/trip x 3,600 trips = 1,440,000 tickets/year (1.44M)
Capacity check: 1.44M / 6.9M = 20.87% — just above the 20% target
math.answer: Yes, at full capacity Uranus can supply 1.44M tickets/year, covering ~20.87% of the market — sufficient to meet the 20% target.

questions.prompt: If Uranus Co. runs at full capacity, will it break even within two years? (Use Exhibit 5)
questions.guidance: Candidate must calculate startup cost (ship construction), annual fixed costs (fuel, maintenance, launch pads, insurance, payroll, marketing), contribution margin per customer, and then solve for breakeven years. Should confirm breakeven < 2 years.

math.setup: Breakeven: Startup cost = [(Contribution margin per ticket x tickets/year) - Annual fixed costs] x number of years
steps: Annual fuel cost: 500,000 gal/trip x 3,600 trips x $5/gal = $9B
Annual launch pad leases: 10 pads x $10M = $100M
Other annual fixed costs: insurance $450M + payroll $40M + marketing $50M = $540M
math.answer: Uranus breaks even in approximately 1.68 years — under the 2-year target.

brainstorming.prompt: What risks and considerations should Uranus Co. be aware of as it enters the space travel market?

categories.name: Regulatory
ideas: International aerospace regulations could change on short notice
Launch pad permits may be difficult to secure globally
Safety certification requirements vary by country

categories.name: Safety & Liability
ideas: Catastrophic failure risk and liability exposure
Insurance claims from accidents could be extremely costly

categories.name: Market & Competitive
ideas: SpaceX and MoonShine could respond aggressively to new entrant
Fragmented market may consolidate around incumbents
Market size estimates based on small, potentially unrepresentative survey

categories.name: Operational
ideas: Setup complexity and lead time to build 150 ships
Hiring specialized pilots, flight attendants, maintenance, and construction crew
Launch pad availability is limited to 10 globally

categories.name: Demand Uncertainty
ideas: Survey of only 200 American millionaires may not reflect global demand
Repeat purchase behavior uncertain after first trip

recommendation: Uranus Co. should enter the luxury space travel market. The total addressable market is approximately 6.9M tickets per year, and Uranus's superior offering across safety, distance, length of voyage, and amenities positions it strongly against fragmented competition.
At full capacity (1.44M tickets/year, ~20.87% market share), Uranus generates sufficient contribution margin to break even in approximately 1.68 years — within the 2-year target.
risks: Regulatory environment could change rapidly, disrupting launch operations
Safety and liability concerns are significant given the nature of space travel
Demand estimates are based on a small, US-only survey sample and may not represent global millionaire demand
Competitor response from SpaceX and MoonShine during the setup period could erode projected market share
$225B upfront capital requirement represents substantial financial risk
next_steps: Conduct additional and broader global market surveys to better validate demand estimates beyond the 200-person US sample
Begin hiring specialized personnel — pilots, flight attendants, maintenance crew, and construction workers — and start building the fleet
Initiate a marketing blitz and begin taking pre-orders in preparation for the maiden voyage
Engage with regulatory bodies across key geographies to secure necessary launch permits and certifications
